hook: A two-solvent electrolyte lets sodium-ion cells run from -50 to 100 C.
hook_turn: lets sodium-ion cells run from -50 to 100 C.

readout.label: Pouch cell capacity retention, 300 cycles at 25 C

summary: Mixing ethyl propionate with a nonflammable phosphazene solvent weakens how tightly sodium ions are held, so they move faster and form a stable electrode film. Prussian blue and hard carbon cells ran across the wide temperature range, and ampere-hour pouch cells kept 86.3% capacity after 300 cycles. Low-temperature and hot pouch runs lasted only about 100 cycles.
title: Hybrid Weakly Coordinated Solvents for Fast-Charging and Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Full Batteries
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
